title: Reimbursement and Billing Manual: Units Covered by a Plan Member Waiver on the CGM Supply Allowance, Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program
content:
# Units covered by a plan member waiver on the CGM supply allowance

Reimbursement and Billing Manual, Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program, Larkfield Medical Supply.

This section fixes the number of billing units of the CGM supply allowance (A4239) that a plan member waiver covers for the next delivery of that item on a Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program enrollment. One billing unit of the CGM supply allowance is one 30-day supply of sensors.

## 1. What the delivery carries

1.1 The next delivery draws on the authorization grant resting on the newest written order of the item, that is, the grant whose underlying written order is the most recently dated written order of the CGM supply allowance on the program (where several grants rest on that order, the one with the latest valid-through date).

1.2 The delivery carries the fewest of three counts of 30-day blocks: (a) the 30-day blocks of one standard shipment, being the tier's standard days of supply per refill shipment divided by 30; (b) the whole 30-day blocks from today through that grant's valid-through date, both days counted, being the number of days from today to the valid-through date plus one, divided by 30 with any remainder dropped (none when the valid-through date has already passed); (c) the whole blocks the program's authorized units remaining allow at the tier's sensor allowance units per 30 days of supply, being the units remaining divided by that allowance with any remainder dropped (none when no units remain).

1.3 With no grant resting on the newest written order, the delivery carries nothing. The delivery's units are its blocks multiplied by the tier's sensor allowance units per 30 days of supply.

## 2. The latest refill and related records

2.1 The latest refill is the refill shipment of the CGM supply allowance on the program with the latest ship date, read for its ship date, supply days, billing route and claim; its claim is the latest claim submission billing that shipment. Its supply counts as paid by the payer for its supply days when it was billed by payer claim, from its ship date; a refill billed to the customer as self-pay carries no paid supply days. The paid-supply end is the latest refill's ship date plus its paid supply days; it is after today when it is a later date than today.

2.2 The payer authorization is the grant the latest refill drew on, its units left being its units less the units of refills drawn on it, never below zero.

2.3 The units beyond the payer authorization are, when the delivery draws on a grant other than the one the latest refill drew on, the delivery's units beyond that authorization's units left, and none otherwise.

2.4 The pump delivery is the pump delivery date recorded on the customer's Insulin Pump Program enrollment, and the over-limit justification is the latest medical record on the CGM program with purpose over-limit justification, dated by the practitioner visit it records.

## 3. The past-due amount

3.1 The hold window is the tier's past-due age in days divided by 30, rounded down, read as a number of whole calendar months. A posting lies within the window when it was posted fewer than that number of whole calendar months before today; when the number is 0, no posting lies within the window.

3.2 The past-due amount is the remittance patient responsibility, patient charges and refunds posted on the program, less those posted within the window, less every payment and balance adjustment posted on the program at any date.

3.3 While an approved payment plan's installments are current, the plan covers the past-due remittance patient responsibility left after those credits, other than the posting named on the latest hardship application on the program: the remittance patient responsibility outside the window, less every payment and balance adjustment posted on the program, less the amount of the posting named on the latest hardship application on the program, never below zero. The plan read is the most recently logged approved payment plan; its installments are current when the patient payments posted on the program fewer whole calendar months before today than one more than the whole calendar months since the plan was logged reach the plan's monthly amount for each whole calendar month since it was logged.

3.4 The uncovered past-due amount is the past-due amount less the amount the plan covers, never below zero; on a tier whose past-due age is 0 days it is zero.

## 4. Whether the delivery can ship today

4.1 The earliest permitted ship date is the tier's refill ship lead days, in calendar days, before the latest refill's ship date plus its supply days.

4.2 The delivery ships only when its earliest permitted ship date is not after today and either the uncovered past-due amount is below the tier's past-due hold minimum or the tier's past-due age is 0 days.

## 5. Units at risk and the count

5.1 When the paid-supply end is after today, every 30-day block of the delivery is at risk; when it is not, no block is at risk. The units at risk are the at-risk blocks multiplied by the tier's sensor allowance units per 30 days of supply.

5.2 The waiver lists the units at risk.

5.3 Each adjustment to this count changes the standard count as that adjustment states, in this order: the earliest ship date and the paid-supply end are moved or replaced first, the at-risk blocks are then marked against the paid-supply end as moved, blocks are then taken off those at-risk blocks, and the listing replaced last; the waiver covers a whole number of units, never below zero, and nothing when the delivery cannot ship today.

5.4 Whole calendar months from one date to a later date are the difference in calendar months between them, less one when the later date's calendar day is earlier than the earlier date's calendar day.

## Worked example (hypothetical figures only)

Suppose the tier's figures were: 60 days of supply per refill shipment, 2 sensor allowance units per 30 days, 5 refill ship lead days, a past-due age of 60 days and a past-due hold minimum of 40.00 USD. Today is a hypothetical 1 June.

| Quantity | Working | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Blocks of one standard shipment | 60 divided by 30 | 2 |
| Blocks through a grant valid through 30 September | 121 days to that date, plus one, is 122; divided by 30, remainder dropped | 4 |
| Blocks allowed by 10 authorized units remaining | 10 divided by 2 | 5 |
| Delivery | fewest of 2, 4 and 5 | 2 blocks, 4 units |
| Latest refill | shipped 5 May by payer claim, 30 days of supply | paid-supply end 4 June |
| Earliest permitted ship date | 4 June less 5 days | 30 May, not after today |
| Hold window | 60 divided by 30 | 2 whole calendar months |
| Past-due amount | remittance patient responsibility of 80.00 posted 10 February counts; a patient charge of 30.00 posted 20 May is within the window; a payment of 50.00 is deducted | 30.00, below 40.00 |
| Units at risk | the paid-supply end is after today, so both blocks are at risk; 2 multiplied by 2 | 4 |

The delivery can ship today and the waiver covers 4 units. Had the remittance posted 10 February been 100.00, the past-due amount would be 50.00, not below 40.00; with no approved payment plan the delivery could not ship today and the waiver would cover nothing.
